entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Fāsī (fl. 1326–1429) was a prominent Maliki qadi and muhaddith in Mecca, Arabia. As a leading authority on Islamic jurisprudence and hadith, his scholarship profoundly impacted the development of Islamic law in the medieval period. His works in hadith collection and juristic scholarship continue to be referenced by scholars today.



Al-Fāsī's tenure as qadi in Mecca involved mediating disputes and overseeing the implementation of Islamic law in the city. His involvement in the governance of Mecca underscores the significant role of Islamic scholars in shaping the legal and social fabric of the city.



The legacy of Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Fāsī extends beyond his immediate contributions to Islamic law. His scholarship played a crucial role in the transmission of knowledge from the 14th to the 16th century, influencing the development of Islamic thought and legal scholarship in the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia.



The significance of Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Fāsī's life can be gauged by the enduring impact of his works on Islamic jurisprudence and the continued relevance of his scholarship in contemporary Islamic scholarship.

entities.summary:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Fasi was an Arab Muslim scholar, muhaddith, faqih (jurist), historian, genealogist, and a Maliki qadi (judge) in Mecca. Born on September 16, 1373, in Mecca, Arabia, he was a member of the prominent Fasi family, known for their contributions to Islamic jurisprudence and hadith authentication. Al-Fasi's magnum opus, 'Al-Zubdat al-Muhaddithin', is a seminal work on the authentication of hadith and remains a crucial reference for scholars to this day.

As a prominent figure in the Islamic Golden Age, al-Fasi played a significant role in the development of Maliki jurisprudence and the establishment of the qadi system in Mecca. He was known for his exceptional knowledge of Islamic law, hadith, and genealogy, which he utilized to authenticate and interpret the hadith of the Prophet Muhammad.

Al-Fasi's legacy extends beyond his own era, as his work has influenced scholars for centuries. His writings on hadith authentication continue to be studied and referenced by scholars around the world, solidifying his place as one of the most important scholars of his time.

The significance of al-Fasi's work cannot be overstated. His contributions to the field of hadith authentication have had a lasting impact on Islamic scholarship, and his legacy continues to shape the way scholars approach the study of the Prophet's words.
